title: Entity Framework Core in one screen
rememberThis: AddDbContext registers scoped DbContext — one per HTTP request, not thread-safe, disposed at scope end.
Reads: AsNoTracking + Select projection to DTO. Writes: tracked load or Attach + SaveChangesAsync.
N+1: detect via SQL log count per request. Fix with projection (best), Include, or AsSplitQuery for multi-collection.
Pagination: cursor/keyset for large feeds; offset OK for small admin tables. COUNT is expensive — skip or cache.
RowVersion concurrency → DbUpdateConcurrencyException → HTTP 409 Conflict. DbContext direct beats generic IRepository<T>.
bullets: DbContext is unit of work + repository — Microsoft recommends direct injection for most APIs.
BackgroundService: IServiceScopeFactory.CreateAsyncScope() per message — never inject DbContext into singleton.
Compiled queries (EF.CompileAsyncQuery) cache plans for identical hot read paths.
Index foreign keys and filter/sort columns — pagination and Include performance depend on indexes.
dotnet-counters ActiveDbContexts should track concurrent requests; stuck at 1 = captive dependency.
TagWith on queries correlates SQL logs to endpoints in staging.
Integration test with SQLite in-memory or Testcontainers — do not mock IRepository for EF confidence.
